translation:
Fix arbitrary types Fm of sentences and S of systems, with logical connectives and constants on Fm and a provability relation for S on Fm. Each definition specifies a property of a system 𝓢 in S and the indicated arbitrary functions from Fm to Fm; it does not assert that the property holds.

Def5(𝓢, D, K): For every sentence φ, if 𝓢 proves φ, then, if 𝓢 proves D(φ), 𝓢 proves K(φ). This is a rule with two provability premises, not a requirement that 𝓢 prove an implication.

Def6(𝓢, D, T): For every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves the implication D(φ) 🡒 (T(φ) 🡘 φ). It need not prove D(φ).

Def7(𝓢, D, T): For every sentence φ and then every sentence ψ, 𝓢 proves the biconditional between D(φ 🡒 ψ) and the conjunction of D(φ) with the implication T(φ) 🡒 D(ψ).

Def8(𝓢, D, K): For every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves the biconditional D(K(φ)) 🡘 D(φ).

In Def6–Def8 the connectives in the sentence to be proved are those of Fm. None of the definitions assumes classicality, consistency, or any of the other defined properties.

divergences.description: Def5 takes separate proofs of φ and D(φ), whereas DK-Intro takes a proof of their conjunction. These presentations are equivalent in the intended classical system, but the Lean definitions do not require conjunction introduction or elimination, or classicality more generally.

Def7 and Def8 require provability of each sentence instance, not a single internally quantified axiom about codes. For D4, typing makes the Sent guards redundant on the represented instances, but proving those instances does not amount to proving the universal axiom.
D7, unlike D4, has no Sent guard. Its arithmetic variable ranges even over numbers that are not sentence codes; Def8 has no instances corresponding to those numbers.

judgement.summary: At the declared sentence level, all four definitions preserve the source formulas and their directions. Def6 in particular matches the conditioned biconditional exactly; the caveats concern the logic needed for the split rule and the scope of the two axiom schemata.
